title: Add `apisever_watch_decode_errors_total` metric to track watch stream decode failures

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: needs-sig
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR lacks a `sig/foo` label and requires one.

labels.name: needs-triage
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR lacks a `triage/foo` label and requires one.

body:
### What happened?

#### Problem statement
Currently, `apiserver_storage_decode_errors_total` only tracks CRUD decode errors. Watch decode errors are unmonitored, making it impossible to validate whether decode errors are caused by unreachable webhook(`conversion_webhook_call_failure`) or potential data corruption.

#### Use Case: Detecting Data Corruption
When investigating decode errors, operators need to distinguish:

1. Webhook-induced decode errors (expected) - webhook validation/mutation failures that prevent proper encoding
2. Potential Data corruption (critical) - actual corruption in etcd or during transmission

#### Detection method
If: webhook_failures == storage_decode_errors + watch_decode_errors
Then: All decode errors are webhook-induced (no data corruption)


If: storage_decode_errors + watch_decode_errors > webhook_failures  
Then: **Potential** Data corruption detected! (decode errors exceed webhook failures)


### What did you expect to happen?

Add `apiserver_watch_decode_errors_total` to complete observability:

```
watchDecodeErrorCounts = compbasemetrics.NewCounterVec(
    &compbasemetrics.CounterOpts{
        Namespace:      "apiserver",
        Name:           "watch_decode_errors_total",
        Help:           "Number of watch event decode errors split by object type",
        StabilityLevel: compbasemetrics.ALPHA,
    },
    []string{"group", "resource"},
)
```
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/8c9c67c000104450cfc5a5f48053a9a84b73cf93/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage/etcd3/watcher.go#L759
```
func decodeObj(codec runtime.Codec, versioner storage.Versioner, data []byte, rev int64, groupResource schema.GroupResource, key string) (_ runtime.Object, err error) {
	obj, err := runtime.Decode(codec, []byte(data))
	if err != nil {
		...
		metrics.RecordWatchDecodeError(groupResource)
		klog.V(2).Infof("Watch decoding %s \"%s\" failed due to %v", groupResource, key, err)
		return nil, err
	}
	...
	return obj, nil
}
```

Benefits:

- Enable corruption detection: Can now validate `conversion_webhook_call_failure` == `total_decode_errors`
- Complete observability: All decode paths are monitored
- Better alerting: Alert on decode_errors > webhook_failures for real corruption



### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Update config to use unexisting webhook to introduce webhook failure

### Anything else we need to know?

_No response_

### Kubernetes version

1.35 (theoretically any version enabled listWatch cacher Decode path)

title: fake.NewClientset should track status and spec independently

labels.name: sig/api-machinery
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG API Machinery.

labels.name: needs-triage
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR lacks a `triage/foo` label and requires one.

body:
### Description

The generated client-go fake clientset (e.g., k8s.io/client-go/kubernetes/fake) does not correctly model the separation between spec and status when using server-side apply.

When the same manager performs:

1. Apply() to update spec-owned fields
2. ApplyStatus() to update status-owned fields

the second call overwrites fields from the first call. This diverges from real apiserver behavior, where spec and status are separate subresources and are merged independently.

### Reproducer

````go
client := NewClientset()
namespace := "default"

pod, err := client.CoreV1().Pods(namespace).Apply(context.Background(),
	v1ac.Pod("foo", namespace).WithFinalizers("foo-finalizer"),
	meta_v1.ApplyOptions{FieldManager: "test-manager"})
require.NoError(t, err)
require.Equal(t, pod.Finalizers, []string{"foo-finalizer"})

pod, err = client.CoreV1().Pods(namespace).ApplyStatus(context.Background(),
	v1ac.Pod("foo", namespace).WithStatus(v1ac.PodStatus().WithPhase(v1.PodPending)),
	meta_v1.ApplyOptions{FieldManager: "test-manager"})
require.NoError(t, err)
require.Equal(t, pod.Status.Phase, v1.PodPending)
require.Equal(t, pod.Finalizers, []string{"foo-finalizer"})
````

### Actual behavior

The second call (ApplyStatus) overwrites the object stored in the fake tracker, causing fields set via Apply() (e.g. metadata.finalizers) to be lost.

This indicates that:

- Apply() and ApplyStatus() are not tracked independently
- The fake client does not model the /status subresource
- Server-side apply merge semantics are not respected

### Expected behavior

The fake client should behave like a real apiserver:

- Apply() updates spec/metadata fields
- ApplyStatus() updates only the status subresource
- Fields written by Apply() must remain intact after ApplyStatus()

This behavior is correctly observed when running the same code against a real API server (e.g. via envtest or a real cluster).

### Why this matters

- Controllers commonly update spec and status in separate calls
- Unit tests using fake.NewClientset produces false failures
- This encourages incorrect controller patterns (single combined updates) to work around fake behavior
- The divergence is subtle and easy to miss

### Notes

The root cause appears to be that the fake client’s ObjectTracker does not implement subresource semantics for /status, even for built-in types that support it.

Should probably be considered as a feature request, as the general advice is to write envtest when real apiserver behavior is required. At the same time, many developers prefer to use fake clients - even for more than just simple unit tests, mainly because a fake client is faster and easier to use/bootstrap.

Follow-up after https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/125560.

For inspiration, this has been "solved" when using the controller-runtime fake client: https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/controller-runtime/pull/2259.
